title: A raw NUL in a comment once hid a modified entrypoint from every content rule
intent: The release prepends a comment holding a raw NUL byte to the package main. Before rules 1.58.0 the sandbox parser classified any file with a NUL as binary and kept no text sample, so no content rule, AI evidence or injection screen saw the code, although Node still runs it. The parser now decodes script source anyway (control bytes shown as U+FFFD) and flags it `control-bytes`; the code rules see the download-and-execute payload and file.control-bytes reports the bytes themselves. The sample is the inert FileRecord the parser produces; the URL is example.invalid.
